description: Digital Museum of Ghost Hardware is a visual archive tracking eight pieces of NASA equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars. It researches and explore real archival imagery, exact engineering specifications, and the operational reality of why each piece of hardware was abandoned. The artifacts that have been analyzed have an interesting story behind them. Some of them have been left behind on purpose while others have remained in space due to external factors.

details: Digital Museum of Ghost Hardware is a visual archive and engineering audit that tracks eight pieces of decommissioned NASA hardware left across the Moon and Mars, organized sequentially by their exact distance from Earth today. Built exclusively with real archival imagery from the NASA/LPI Apollo Image Atlas, NSSDCA, and JPL Photojournal alongside telemetry from the Catalogue of Manmade Material on the Moon (RP-1097), the exhibit documents each asset's hardware specifications, exact locations, and the operational reason it was abandoned. By analyzing how 14-ton Saturn V rocket stages were repurposed into seismic kinetic impactors, how Surveyor 3 served as the first multi-year vacuum degradation audit, and how the grounded Ingenuity rotorcraft was patched via firmware into a 20-year stationary weather logger, the project demonstrates that discarded aerospace equipment does not become dead space junk—it evolves into permanent scientific infrastructure.
